absent: Locking and concurrency rules for TTBR, ASID, PLT and VMA helpers are not shown.
Page-table entry formats, TLB maintenance internals and fault handling beyond flush calls are not shown.
Physical memory discovery, boot mapping creation and swapper reservation use are not shown.
MTE, POE, BTI, GCS and KPTI hardware enable sequences beyond thin aliases are not shown.
52-bit address and tagged-address ABI edge cases beyond the given helpers are not shown.

findings.text: High virtual address map is top-relative: configured VA width defines the linear base, kernel image starts where modules end, module window is 2 GiB, vmemmap ends 1 GiB below top, PCI IO follows vmemmap, fixed map tops 8 MiB below top.
Minimum VA width has build variants around 47 and 48 or tracking configured width; the half address boundary and kernel start and end sentinels derive from it.

KASAN shadow window uses a configured offset plus scale-derived size anchored at top of address space; linear top follows shadow start when enabled and otherwise follows the half boundary, with a one-bit thread size bump when KASAN is active.

Thread and stack geometry: minimum thread order is 14 plus KASAN bump, thread order and size derive from page order, alignment is twice thread size, IRQ stack equals thread size, overflow is 4 KiB, non-VHE stacks are page sized with a combined trace bound, segments align to 64 KiB.

Stage-1 memory type codes are small integers for normal, tagged normal, non-cacheable normal and two device variants; stage-2 has separate legacy and FWB encodings; ioremap largest block is PUD or PMD depending on build; reserved and trampoline swapper slots are one and two pages.

Memblock accepts the full 64-bit range; physical frame offset derives from physical base; initial memblock tables scale from a base count with per-CPU and multiplier terms; T0SZ encodes 64 minus VA width shifted into place; AArch32 context flag is bit 0 and user ASID marker is bit 48.
Process MM context holds an atomic ASID, optional compat signal page, pin count, VDSO pointer, flags word and a byte-sized protection-key allocation map.

Module arch state tracks core and init PLT section index, used entries and capacity, plus separate executable trampoline areas for normal and init for dynamic tracing; each PLT slot is three little-endian instruction words using a call-scratch register as veneer.
TCR is read with a direct system-register move; effective VA width is either decoded from hardware state or fixed to the configured width depending on build.

Address conversion family distinguishes linear-map addresses from kernel-image addresses by range, then applies the matching base adjustment; helpers cover phys and virt directions, symbol addresses, frame numbers, page structures with tag preservation, and validity checking via range plus mapped-memory test.

Pointer tagging helpers clear or manipulate the top byte by sign extension and shifts when memory tagging is enabled and become identities or zero when disabled; one helper replaces the tag field while preserving low bits.

Arch tag-check controls are thin aliases for lower-layer memory-tagging operations covering synchronous, asynchronous, asymmetric and store-only modes, temporary suppression, async fault checks, random tags and per-address tag access.
KASLR helpers report image displacement from its link base and whether randomization is active, with a no-op init and a disabled-build variant that always reports false.

Mmap policy hooks translate branch-target and memory-tagging protection requests into VM flags only when hardware supports them, mark anonymous or suitable shared mappings as tag-capable, accept only the supported protection set, and reject tag-enabled mappings lacking prior allowance.

Shadow-stack validation rejects executable shadow stacks and warns on shared ones; VMA permission checks consult the overlay permission register per key for read, write and execute unless the access is foreign or the feature is absent.
Per-process MM setup zeroes the ASID and pin count and reserves key zero; fork duplicates the key map; exit and unmap hooks exist but do no work in these fragments.

Context switching updates saved user base for the incoming task even when the address space pointer is unchanged; lazy TLB points the saved user base at the initial address space; deactivation releases the shadow-stack mapping.

CPU mask helpers restrict 32-bit threads to capable CPUs when the system is mismatched, otherwise return the normal possible mask; the system query returns none, the 32-bit subset or all CPUs according to support and mismatch state.

Reserved mapping helpers install or remove an identity map with TLB flush and user-size update, install an arbitrary user base without full switch semantics, enable sharedness on the kernel base, and replace the kernel base with an early-only wrapper that warns after capabilities finalize.

KPTI-related helpers decide whether randomization needs isolation based on hardware mitigation availability and provide an empty install hook in this configuration; untag mask exposes all but the top byte.
Module helpers locate an ELF section by name through the string table and report whether a PLT site falls in a narrow trailing range affected by an address erratum when that workaround is active.

Linear membership is a range check against linear base and top; symbol and image translations use the image offset while linear translations use physical start, and debug variants bypass extra checking.
Page-to-address conversions preserve KASAN tags on both the generic phys-based path and the direct vmemmap-indexed path; reverse conversion recomputes the descriptor address from the untagged index.

User-size updates are skipped when already set, otherwise rewrite the register field and order with a barrier; identity-map removal restores the normal user size and conditionally restores the previous user table.

Protection-key extraction shifts arch key flag bits down by a fixed shift; overlay permission checks select read, write or execute predicates in priority order with write and execute taking precedence over read.
Kernel-base replacement runs as install identity map, mask asynchronous events, call the physical replacement routine with the new base plus sharing bit, restore masking, then uninstall identity map.
Shadow-stack teardown is gated on feature support and current address space, then unmaps the recorded region if present and clears pointer, base and size state.

Arch MM switch entry handles cross-address-space switch plus saved-base refresh; identity-map install and uninstall and TCR user-size update are the low-level entries used around early or replacement mapping changes.

TCR is read without the usual volatile system-register helper, so callers must not assume compiler ordering beyond the explicit move; replacement path explicitly masks events because faults during base replacement are unsafe.

Early base replacement after capability finalization is a programming error and warns; PLT placement near the end of a page can be forbidden on affected CPUs and must be checked before emitting the veneer.
